PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 11, round 2. Audited at 34b7da1 (the merge of devteam2/sprint-11
into main), whose tree is cb57b249e52d4b68183dc1a56520bb4c3433b73c. Sprint file
re-read fresh immediately before this verdict.

VERDICT: PASS.

WHY THERE IS A ROUND 2, and it is not the sprint's fault. Two things changed since
round 1, one of them mine:

1. The sprint file gained a Team Assignments correction, applied at my
   recommendation, which correctly tripped the dev-done hash check. I diffed the
   file against its last committed form: the only content change is the appended
   "Corrected 16 Aug 2026" block recording that Dev Team 2 built this sprint and
   owns the remaining lifecycle commands. Accurate, dated, and in the project's
   existing amendment convention. Nothing in Requirements, Acceptance Criteria, or
   Out of Scope moved, so round 1's coverage stands unchanged.

2. Round 1's PASS recorded the wrong tree hash, and that was my error. I ran
   /sprint-qa1 from the main checkout while auditing a commit on a branch, and
   sprint_lifecycle.py line 475 records git_tree_hash("HEAD") -- the checkout's HEAD,
   not the commit under review. So it stamped main's tree (85eb30e78..., = a499612)
   rather than the audited content (cb57b249...). /sprint-ship compares the shipped
   commit's tree against that value and refuses on mismatch, so no commit carrying
   this sprint's content could ever have shipped against that verdict. Merging the
   branch into main first, so HEAD is the audited content, fixes it at the source.
   This round records cb57b249..., which is the tree Pipeman will actually ship.

The merge itself is content-neutral: git diff --stat 344d12b HEAD is empty, and the
merged tree equals 344d12b's tree exactly. So this re-audit is genuinely
proportionate -- not one line of code differs from what I passed in round 1.

Requirements coverage: R1 through R5 and the ordering criterion all MET, exactly as
recorded in round 1. Those findings were established against 344d12b, whose content
is byte-identical to what I am stamping now, including the live probes:
- GET / returned 307 to /chart, and following it served the chart page. Framework
  level, via next.config.ts redirects(), permanent: false for 307 rather than a
  hard-cached 308.
- /api/health/db returned commit: { sha, short, isLocal } in the down branch
  ("344d12babcdef0123456" / "344d12b" / false) and in the misconfigured branch
  ("local-dev" / "local-dev" / true), confirming both forms and that the local
  fallback fires rather than merely surviving as dead code.
- ec522b0's file list confirms the ordering criterion: the SHA arrives in the health
  route and app/page.tsx is deleted in the same commit, so no shipped state exists
  without a deployed-commit observable.
- RUNBOOK's three stale homepage references are all updated to /api/health/db's
  commit.sha.

Re-verified against the merged tree at 34b7da1:
- lint exits 0. Tests exit 0, 70 across 7 files. next build exits 0, and the route
  table has no / at all, confirming no orphaned route.
- Rebuilt with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY="QA1PROBESERVICEROLE" and grepped all of

- Typecheck: see note 1. It failed on my first pass and it is not a defect.

Notes, not conditions:
1. Deleting a route makes a stale .next hostile, and I walked into it myself. My
   first `npm run typecheck` against the merged tree failed with
     .next/types/validator.ts(62,39): error TS2307:
       Cannot find module '../../app/page.js'
   That file is generated by a previous build, from back when app/page.tsx existed,
   and tsconfig's include pulls in .next/types/**/*.ts. It is a stale artifact, not
   a code problem. Verified two ways: `rm -rf .next && npm run typecheck` exits 0,
   and a pristine `git archive HEAD` export with no .next present -- which is exactly
   what a CI checkout looks like -- gives tsc exit 0 and eslint exit 0. CI is not
   affected; the build job runs on a fresh checkout every time. But anyone who pulls
   this change into a working directory that already has a .next will get an error
   naming a file this sprint deliberately deleted, and will reasonably conclude the
   sprint broke typechecking. `rm -rf .next` clears it. Worth a line in the README or
   the sprint handoff, because the failure message points at exactly the wrong thing.
2. Tooling gap, already raised and still standing: the Dev Team 2 worktree workflow
   and /sprint-ship's tree-content check do not compose, because /sprint-qa1 records
   the auditing checkout's HEAD rather than the commit reviewed. Sprints 1 through 10
   were all built on main, so this could not surface until Sprint 11 -- the first
   sprint actually built on a branch. Either /sprint-qa1 takes an explicit --commit
   and records that commit's tree, or it is documented that a branch-built sprint
   lands on local main before its audit. Per CLAUDE.md that is a change to this
   repository's own tooling and does not go through a sprint. Master Controller's
   call. Recording it here so the reasoning survives past this conversation.
3. I deliberately did not reach for --gate ship-hash to unstick round 1's bad tree
   hash. It would have worked, and it is the wrong instrument: it is a human
   override, permanently written into the sprint's history as one, and using it to
   paper over an audit recorded against the wrong baseline would put a false signal
   in the record. The override log is worth something only if it contains real
   overrides. Same reasoning for --gate dev-done-hash on the sprint-file amendment --
   a fresh audit re-stamps that hash as a side effect of being done properly.
4. Per the sprint file's own correction, Dev Team 2 owns /sprint-dev-done 11 and
   /sprint-complete 11 from here, run from the main checkout. The worktree's
   duplicate state file and sprint file have been deleted, so there is one copy of
   sprint 11's state and it is the one this verdict was written into.

PASS: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 11, commit
34b7da137efd00a2c587fb1e19ea2f6f4cebe2b5.
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-08-16 ~20:10Z.

VERDICT: PASS. All three criteria verified.

This sprint replaces the instrument I have used to verify every deploy since
Sprint 1 -- the commit SHA rendered on the root page -- with a field in
/api/health/db. So I tested the replacement harder than the criteria strictly
require, because if it is wrong or stale-able, every future live test inherits the
fault silently.

CRITERION 1 -- GET / returns a redirect to /chart, and following it serves the
chart page. PASS.
  GET / -> HTTP/2 307, location: /chart
  Response body is 15 bytes. It is a real redirect, not a rendered page with a
  link on it, which is what R2 asked for.
  Following it -> final_status 200, final_url
  https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app/chart, serving the chart page:
    "Planetary positions | Geocentric planetary positions for a past date. No
     account required to view them - save one and anyone with the link can open
     it. | Date | Cast | Supported range: 1700-01-01 to 2100-12-31"

  On R3 (permanent by intent, but not cached so aggressively it cannot be
  changed): the status is 307, not 308, and the response carries
  cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate. That combination is the
  cautious reading of R3 -- a 308 is a permanent redirect that browsers cache
  durably and are reluctant to forget, which is exactly the trap R3 names. Nothing
  here will be stuck in a user's cache if the destination changes.

  Bonus behaviour, not required by any criterion but worth recording because it
  will matter: the redirect preserves the query string.
    GET /?date=1969-07-20 -> 307, location: /chart?date=1969-07-20
  So an old link to the root carrying a date still lands somewhere useful rather
  than dropping the parameter.
  HEAD / behaves identically (307 -> /chart). // returns 308 (path
  normalisation, Vercel's own, not the app's).

CRITERION 2 -- /api/health/db reports the deployed commit SHA and it matches what
Pipeman shipped. PASS. This is the sprint's actual proof.
  GET /api/health/db, body verbatim:
    {"status":"ok","connected":true,
     "migrationVersion":"20260816181929_readings_positions_not_null",
     "commit":{"sha":"34b7da137efd00a2c587fb1e19ea2f6f4cebe2b5",
               "short":"34b7da1","isLocal":false}}
  - sha matches Pipeman's shipped commit and origin/main exactly, all 40
    characters: 34b7da137efd00a2c587fb1e19ea2f6f4cebe2b5.
  - Both forms present as R1 requires: full sha and short (34b7da1), and short is
    genuinely the first 7 of full rather than an independently-derived value.
  - isLocal is false, which is correct on production and shows the local
    development fallback is not firing where it should not.
  - Note this is a MERGE commit (34b7da1 merges devteam2/sprint-11). The deploy
    hook path reports the merge SHA correctly, which is the case most likely to go
    wrong and did not.

  STALENESS CHECK, beyond the criterion. The whole value of this observable is
  that it cannot lie about what is deployed, so I checked whether a cached copy
  could:
    cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate
    x-vercel-cache: MISS, age: 0
    Three consecutive fetches with NO cache-buster returned byte-identical
    payloads with the correct SHA.
  It is not being served from an edge cache, and max-age=0 means a future test
  cannot be handed a stale SHA the way the Sprint 1 page could (that page returned
  x-vercel-cache: HIT with age: 777 on one of my earlier runs, which is precisely
  the failure mode I warned about at the time). The replacement is a better
  instrument than the thing it replaces, not merely an equivalent one.

CRITERION 3 -- the old proof page is gone: no route serves it. PASS. I went
looking rather than accepting that / redirects.
  Probed /, /index, /index.html, /home, /page, /proof, /?x=1, // -- and grepped
  every response for the old proof page's distinctive strings ("reaches production
  without hand-holding", "Deployed commit:"). Zero hits on all eight.
    / -> 307, /index -> 404, /index.html -> 404, /home -> 404, /page -> 404,
    /proof -> 404, /?x=1 -> 307, // -> 308
  Also grepped the served /chart page and the followed-redirect response for the
  old <code title="[40 hex]"> SHA marker: 0 occurrences anywhere. The marker I
  have been reading since Sprint 1 is genuinely gone from the HTML, not merely
  moved off the root.

REGRESSION CHECK -- /chart still works after the change. /chart?date=2024-03-20
still renders the positions table (Sun, Aries present). Removing app/page.tsx did
not disturb the page the root now points at.

NOTE FOR MY OWN FUTURE TESTS, and for anyone reading this later. From this commit
onward the deployed-commit observable is
/api/health/db -> .commit.sha, NOT a code element on the root page. Any live test
written against the old marker will find nothing and, depending on how it is
written, may silently pass. R5's requirement that README record this exists for
exactly that reason. I have verified the new observable end to end and will use it
from here.

TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. All checks
are curl over HTTPS against production. I confirmed the redirect at the HTTP level
and confirmed the destination serves the chart page, but I have not observed the
redirect in a real browser, and I have not observed layout.
